en årring.explanation: "En årring" means "a tree ring". To say how to find the age of a tree, use "tælle" (to count): "Man tæller årringene for at finde træets alder" (You count the tree rings to find the age of the tree).

en årsag.explanation: "En årsag" means "a reason", as in the cause of something. To name a cause, say: "Årsagen til branden er ukendt" (The reason for the fire is unknown). Do not mix it up with "en grund" (a reason). To give a reason for doing something, use "grund": "Jeg har en god grund til at blive hjemme" (I have a good reason to stay home).

en årsopgørelse.explanation: "En årsopgørelse" means "an annual tax statement". It is built from "år" (year) and "opgørelse" (statement). A fact about Denmark: the Danish tax authorities send one to every taxpayer.

en årstid.explanation: "En årstid" means "a season". To name your favorite, say: "Efteråret er min yndlingsårstid" (Autumn is my favorite season). Do not mix it up with "en sæson" (a season of a show or sport): "Sæsonen starter i dag" (The season starts today).

et åbent hus.explanation: "Et åbent hus" means "an open house". When a house is for sale and buyers may visit, it also means "an open house": "Der er åbent hus søndag klokken to" (There is an open house on Sunday at two o'clock).

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". To say your age, add "gammel" (old): "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

et århundrede.explanation: "Et århundrede" means "a century". It is built from "år" (year) and "hundrede" (hundred). To name a period, use a number with a dot: "i det 21. århundrede" (in the 21st century).

et årstal.explanation: "Et årstal" means "a year (date)". To say that a number is a year: "1990 er et årstal" (1990 is a year). Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year as a length of time). To say how long: "tre år" (three years).

et årti.explanation: "Et årti" means "a decade". To name a decade, add "-erne" to the number: "firserne" (the eighties).

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open". To talk about the action, use the verb "at åbne" (to open): "Jeg åbner døren" (I open the door).

åbenbart.explanation: "Åbenbart" means "apparently". It comes from the word "åbenbar" (obvious). To say you have just noticed something, say: "Du har åbenbart ikke hørt det" (You have apparently not heard it).

åbenlys.explanation: "Åbenlys" means "obvious". It is built from "åben" (open) and "lys" (light). To say something is clearly true, say: "Det er åbenlyst, at hun har ret" (It is obvious that she is right).

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "tider" (times).

åndelig.explanation: "Åndelig" means "spiritual". It comes from "en ånd" (a spirit). To say someone looks for spiritual help, say: "Han søger åndelig vejledning" (He seeks spiritual guidance). Do not mix it up with "psykisk" (mental). To talk about the mind, say: "Hun har psykiske problemer" (She has mental problems).

årlig.explanation: "Årlig" means "annual". To say how often something happens, use "årligt" (annually): "Det sker årligt" (It happens every year).

årvågen.explanation: "Årvågen" means "alert". The last part, "vågen" (awake), also stands alone: "Jeg er vågen" (I am awake).

at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat (of animals)". To say an animal eats, say: "Løven æder kød" (The lion eats meat). For people, use "at spise" (to eat): "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch). Said about a person, "æde" sounds coarse.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change / alter". To say someone has a new opinion, say: "Hun har ændret mening" (She has changed her mind). To swap one thing for another, use "at skifte" (to change, to swap): "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires).

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something". To ask for permission to change a part, say: "Må jeg ændre på teksten?" (May I change the text?) To become different by itself, use "at ændre sig" (to change): "Vejret ændrer sig" (The weather is changing).

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change". To say a person is different now, say: "Hun har ændret sig meget" (She has changed a lot). To change something else, leave out "sig": "Jeg ændrer planen" (I change the plan).

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed". To say what annoys you, add "over" (about): "Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent" (I am annoyed that I was late).

en æblekage.explanation: "En æblekage" means "an apple dessert". A fact about Denmark: it is made of stewed apple, crumbs and whipped cream layered in a glass. It is built from "æble" (apple) and "kage" (cake), but it is not baked as a cake.

en æggejagt.explanation: "En æggejagt" means "an egg hunt". It is built from "æg" (egg) and "jagt" (hunt).

en æggemad.explanation: "En æggemad" means "an egg open sandwich". A fact about Denmark: it is a slice of bread with sliced boiled egg on top. The word "mad" also ends "en ostemad" (a cheese sandwich).
